title: Elastic Context Gateway and Loss-Resilient Trace Hooks
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem statement: external and edge clients (mobile SDKs, browser websockets, legacy proxies) often send partial or reordered trace/context headers. Current SDK middleware rejects or fragments traces which degrades downstream latency dashboards and increases orphan spans. We need a lightweight in-path gateway and SDK hook set that can: 1) accept partial/fragmented carriers, 2) coalesce and canonicalize disparate headers into a stable canonical context, 3) opportunistically reconstruct missing fields using provenance stamps, and 4) apply loss-resilient sampling and tagging so dashboards and SLO alerts maintain fidelity without increasing telemetry cost. This ticket implements the runtime gateway component plus SDK trace-hook adapters for Node/Python/Go SDKs.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Gateway accepts at least three common malformed/partial carrier patterns observed in production (split x-trace-id/x-span, truncated baggage, missing traceparent) and emits a canonical context header set.
2) SDK hooks can attach provenance stamps and best-effort ID mappings without blocking request path (latency p99 < existing baseline + 2ms).
3) Sampling policy respects configured heuristics (error-rates, latency windows) and emits sampling_reason field.
4) End-to-end test against synthetic traffic reproduces prior fragmentation and shows >95% successful stitch rate for multihop requests.
5) Rollout plan documented and feature toggle exists for safe rollback.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1: prototype gateway that runs as edge sidecar (nginx lua for quick iteration) to parse and normalize incoming carriers.
Phase 2: implement language-specific SDK trace hooks that: 1) read canonical headers, 2) add provenance stamp when reconstructing IDs, 3) apply sampling hints.
Phase 3: add kernel-level perf tests and integrate gateway into test harness, then staged rollout behind kill-switch.
Work items: prototype, SDK adapters (node/python/go), unit+integration tests, perf bench, rollout playbook.
Owners: Marcus Li (runtime), Asha Kapoor (SDK), Priya Nambiar (QA).
technical_notes:
- Use a compact provenance stamp: base62(timestamp|node-id|rand4) appended to baggage to avoid extra headers.
- Canonical header mapping table will prefer W3C traceparent if present, then Redwood legacy X-RW-* headers, then heuristics from carrier fingerprints.
- Gateway must be idempotent for repeated normalization.
- Sampling decisions should annotate traces with sampling_reason and sample_priority to enable downstream aggregation.
- Avoid expensive crypto in hot path; use fast CRC32 for quick integrity hint and store full verification hooks for background jobs.
- Backwards compatibility: honor existing SDKs by emitting both canonical and legacy headers during a transition window.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for header parsing and normalization matrix (200+ permutations).
- Integration test that spins up gateway sidecar + SDK client + mock backend and verifies stitched traces in test telemetry pipeline.
- Perf microbench: measure added latency on Node/Python/Go SDKs across 10k requests with varying payload sizes.
- Canary rollout: route 1% of infra traffic through gateway and validate stitch rate and p99 latency.
- Monitoring: add dashboard panels for reconstruct_rate, dropped_carriers, added_latency_p50/p95/p99, and sampling_reason distribution.
